rationale: C22 is a concrete, material drafting template for the child. It uses nearly identical language to identify the same maritime employers, the same four-part employer classification, Atlantic and Gulf Coast operations, the International Longshoremen's Association (Independent), an ongoing strike imperiling national health and safety, and the same Board of Inquiry reporting and continuation machinery. The child principally updates the geographic endpoint, report date, and factual statement concerning perishable products. C17 and C02 share the same structure and much of the specialized maritime language, but concern the narrower North Atlantic region and are less exact matches.

shared_material.child_excerpt: employers (or associations by which such employers are represented in collective bargaining conferences) who are (1) steamship companies or who are engaged as operators or agents for ships engaged in service from or to Atlantic and Gulf coast ports ... (2) contracting stevedores, (3) contracting marine carpenters, or (4) other employers engaged in related or associated pier activities
shared_material.parent_excerpt: employers (or associations by which such employers are represented in collective bargaining conferences) who are (1) steamship companies or who are engaged as operators or agents for ships engaged in service from or to Atlantic and Gulf Coast ports ... shared_material.explanation: Distinctive, nearly verbatim four-part classification of maritime employers and geographic scope.
